From: Derek Morgan, LANCS.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thanks for Issue 45.The new-look
display (SAM version)is not bad,
in fact I could go on to say it
is wonderful or even megafantas-
tic, but you would only get big-
headed and not get through the
door for a week.

Yes!, I loved it. As ever you've
done a great job on Outlet; even
the Tabloid print option now
works for me.
                       - Derek

Moi? Big-headed? Don't be silly,
I'm much too mature to become
vain -I'm far above that sort of
thing.                  - Brian

From Ted Wilson, SURREY

Dear Brian & Ron,

Glad to have met you both at the
All Formats Fair in London.

A number of points to make...

1) Possessing, as I do, all your
OUTLETs since the beginning, is
it possible,without a great deal
of effort, to transfer all the
earlier OUTLETs from m/d to SAM
disc?My first SAM disc is No.40.

2) I have managed, through the
use of Specmaker and Masterdos,
to transfer a lot of my extens-
ive data on family trees on
Masterfile from m/d as well as
Swiftdisc to SAM.

We are told that by using the
RAM disc that full use of the
extra memory of SAM can be made.
However with Masterfile this
does not appear possible without
changes to Masterfile. Does any-
one know how to do this?

I really like Masterfile and
have yet to meet another data-
base to compare with its display
and use of colour. I have con-
tacted their suppliers, Campbell
Systems, who inform me that they
have no intention to modify the
program to suit SAM owners.

3) Any joy with modifications to
ECLECTIC?
               - Dr. E.J.Wilson

Brian Cavers to Ted Wilson

1. It's nearly impossible to
transfer all the early OUTLETS
- even WITH a lot of effort! It
is possible to convert SOME of
the individual programs but each
one needs special attention. In
general, all the code REMs and
line 8940 (FAILSAFE OFF) need
removing. The first SAM is No.32
but if you convert 32 to 39 from
microdrive they would not be the
same as the SAM equivalents. In
EVERY issue there are programs I
am unable to convert and there
are lots of SAM-specific items -
not only to replace these but
added as well! The SAM OUTLET is
usually over 700K - FOUR TIMES
AS BIG AS THE MICRODRIVE
VERSION!

2. MASTERFILE saves its data as
one giant string variable. This
is restricted to the maximum
size allowable in the Spectrum
memory with the BASIC and code
added - about 30K I think. There
is no way to expand this without
a major re-write of the code.

I do not have Specmaker and do
not know how it interacts with
Spectrum programs but I think it
lets you use microdrive syntax
to save to RAM disc instead of
to microdrive or disc.Presumably
there is some option to save the
RAM disc to the real disc later?
This use of memory is only like
having an extra fast drive - it
cannot let your programs grow in
size.

3. Regrettably, I am, as ever,so
overwhelmed with the workload
that I cannot keep up with the
daily essentials of producing
OUTLET. Projects like ECLECTIC
are in a huge box (yes, a BOX
not a tray) that is half full of
densely packed bits and pieces
and notes and info and which I
despair of ever tackling. It is
now nearly 11.00pm Saturday
night - a normal 14-hour, 7-day
week. I can see no solution to
the problem I'm afraid!

                        - Brian

From P.I. Quanstrom, EASTBOURNE

I've an Epson-compatible printer
- a Mannesman Tally MT-80 but am
unable to print out FLASH or
your advert "OUTWRITE!". All I
get is a garbage print-out.

I have a SAM 512K with SAMBUS.

I find that I'm getting problems
with Tasword II, i.e., after
saving, the message appears: "93
verify failed,1470:4".Of course,
there seems to be no real prob-
lem as all that is necessary to
return to the program is to type
GO TO 10.

Does OUTWRITE work with MASTER-
DOS? I'm sure it does.

Brian Cavers to P.I. Quanstrom


Reset your SAM, boot SAMDOS (use
this OUTLET disc if you have no
other copy),load Tasword and try
to save a file. If it works O.K.
then the fault is with MASTERDOS
and it's likely you've an early
version. Contact your supplier
for an upgrade.

If, however, the fault occurs
under SAMDOS as well then there
is probably a fault in line 1470
of the Tasword BASIC. I have the
Spectrum Tasword 2 running under
LERMTAPE so I cannot say what
should be on the line. Let me
know the full line in this case
and I'll advise further.

Regarding your printer, read the
next letter from Colin Demaline.
It seems, hopefully, to be just
what you need.

Yes, OUTWRITE does works with
MASTERDOS although there is no
provision for loading from sub-
directories. I'll make a note to
look into this for the upgrade
version.
                     - Brian

From: Colin Demaline, LANCS.


GRAPHIC DUMPS ON SHINWA CPA80's
& Other Double-Density Printers.
--------------------------------

Pokes first - waffle later...

        DUMP and "dumpld"

Immediately after loading MGT's
"dumpld" OR just before giving a
DUMP command....

        POKE SVAR 31,4
        POKE SVAR 35,75

Changing that final 75 to a 76
will give a double-density half-
width dump.

     "FLASH" - ALL DUMPS
Load "Flash" and at the "Save to
Tape?" prompt DELETE left-hand
quote and enter "STOP". Now
enter....
      POKE 83241,0,27,75
      POKE 83249,0,27,75

Press CONTINUE (F5) and "Save to
Tape/Disc?" prompts appear but I
suggest you DO NOT re-save yet -
not until you are completely
happy with the pokes.
   -   -   -   -   -   -   -
These pokes have been thoroughly
tested with both a 512k and a
256k SAM, the latter with a 1meg
extension and I strongly expect
them to work equally well with
other "Epson-compatible" double-
density printers. Note my use of

quotes on the "Epson-compatible"
bit... as there are even Epsons
which aren't "Epson-compatible"
is it any wonder there is so
much confusion about the matter?

A lot of the confusion arises
because of the large group of
double-density printers which
are "compatible" in all respects
except those commands which are
specifically quad-density. The
Shinwa CP80 series fall in this
group and I believe the Mannes-
man MT80 is another.

The significant command missing
from this group is the ESC 27,
"*",mode command... the double-
density printers are restricted
to ESC "K" and "L" - single and
double density, 8-bit graphics.

Unfortunately, both "dumpld" and
"FLASH" rely on the "*" command,
as does Steve Nutting's "Filer"
(incidentally, "Filer" is THE
definitive database - far above
anything yet produced for the
SAM coupe... or the Spectrum).

However back to the subject...
the pokes above deal with FLASH
and "dumpld" and as "Filer" uses
the latter it is an easy task to
convert it.  There are two BASIC
programs... so just load "auto",
enter BASIC, edit line 12100 and
immediately following the LOAD
"dump" CODE add...
:POKE SVAR 31,4: POKE SVAR 35,75

Re-Enter the line and SAVE OVER
"auto" LINE 65000.

The 2nd BASIC file is "create"
and the same two POKES are added
to line 120, again following the
LOAD "dump" CODE. This time SAVE
OVER "create" LINE 10.

I don't know about the Mannesman
group of printers but the Shinwa
CPA80s have a single dot density
of 80 per inch compared with the
Epson's 60 and this gives a dump
which is about 25% narrow. This
can be offset by having smaller
line-feeds. I haven't, as yet,
solved this problem with the
"dumpld" code but "FLASH" can be
amended at the same time as the
previous pokes....
   POKE 83238,27,51,n
   POKE 83246,27,51,n
when "n" is the number of 216ths
required for each line feed.

The present feed is the equiva-
lent of 24 but I suggest 22 -try
21 as well. I must warn however
that the overprinting of just 2
or 3/216ths can mar the finished
appearance of certain intricate
patterns so use this with care.


This final poke will be useful
with both quad-density and
double-density printers alike.
Have you noticed that before a
"FLASH" dump is made the printer
feeds up three lines. If you
wish to stop, or even reduce,
this feed just add the following
poke with the others. It is...

    POKE 83235,0,0,0

If you wish only to get rid of
two of the feeds, leaving just
the one, then poke only two of
the 0's (or poke one only and
leave two line-feeds).


NOTE...  ALL THE 0s QUOTED IN
THIS ARTICLE ARE THE FIGURE "0".


I can't finish without a mention
of the part played in sorting
out these printer dump problems
by a SAM-owning friend who lives
nearby and visits me regularly.
He is Fred Hindle and the pair
of us have been trying for well
a year to find an answer to our
problems.

We had both of us spoken to Alan
Miles & Bruce Gordon at MGT on
several occasions but were given
only pokes and hints which were
useless. I had also been in
touch with Steve Nutting on a
couple of occasions - all to no
avail. Finally, as a last resort
Fred wrote to Dr. Andy Wright
who put us on the right track by
providing the addresses to
search. We really are grateful
Dr. Andy, thank-you.

I can't close without thanking
M/s. Ron & Brian Cavers for a
terrific magazine. I only hope
that this contribution will go
just a little way towards repay-
ing all the help and enjoyment
that you two (and others) have
given to us, Thank you both.

I know of four SAM owners within
a mile of here and our combined
ages are above 260 yrs. (no - we
weren't born in 1731... it was
just after). Three of us are
subscribers to OUTLET - The
Three Wise Men... but not so old
when we have OUTLET.

        - Colin Demaline




Excellent help and advice there.
Many thanks!
                        - Brian

From D.A. Turton, LIVERPOOL



Can you please tell me how to
format a disk to 203K,as in your
issues on Plus 3 - or is it a
trade secret?

Also, could you tell me what
issue do the +3 versions of
OUTLET start from and whether or
not the tape versions will save
to disk without any problems?

               - D.A. Turton

Brian Cavers to D.A. Turton

Yes, HIFORMAT(OUTLET 35)does the
203K format.

The +3 versions of OUTLET start
at No.23.

The tape version will not run on
disc without changing the LOAD""
to the full name of the next
item (usually line 8920) and
even then files will only load
in sequence - there will be no
random access as with the disc
version. I must also add that I
have never tried the above so it
could be that there may be some
other problem I can't foresee.
There may be programs that will
crash in 128K mode for example.

However, in principle, it should
be possible to get it on disc.If
you attempt an issue note that
"TEXTLOADER" would need to be
saved several times under diff-
erent names (say, TEXT1, TEXT2)
and, generally speaking, you can
use line 9983 to reSAVE.

                        - Brian

From: Ian Kennedy - BOTSWANA



Dear Ron and Brian,


 MASTERDOS AND SPECMAKER/SAMSPEC

I have not been able to get
Specmaker to work with my "Last
Word" tape(Both my tape versions
of Tasword 2 have "walked"). It
just locks up. The same with
"Wordmaster" from Plus D disc.
Also the two Spec emulator
programs and SAM version of Tas-
word 2 seem not to work properly
or not at all with Masterdos but
only with SAMDOS 2.

I am waiting for"Messenger"which
I was hoping might be reviewed
in the latest OUTLET. It is not
clear exactly what "Messenger"
actually does but I have got in
the habit of ordering everything
as it comes out so I am likely
to have a lot of software for
sale soon.

In keeping with my usual experi-
ence, nothing works first time
around even after endless
readings of the manual. I shall
be writing to LERM and SD but
thought you might know of others
who are having problems. I just
cannot spare the time to sit for
hours trying to sort out what
the problem is. Things must work
properly from the start or they
are no use to me.

I am writing this on a Z88 since
I haven't the heart to go back
to my Speccy/Disciple after
trying to convert to SAM.It is a
bit ironic that most of the SAM
effort is still going on trying
to make it a Speccy rather than
branching out on its own.

However, OUTLET keeps me happy
while waiting for these other
things to sort themselves out.

           Sincerely,

           Ian Kennedy

Brian Cavers to Ian Kennedy

Why not use OUTWRITE? You can
still send us 64-column text
files until the variable margin
version arrives. MESSENGER plugs
SAM and Spectrum together by a
cable. You load your program in
the Spectrum then press a button
and the whole of memory, ROM
included, is passed to the SAM.
You can save the resulting"snap-
shot" on SAM disc. However,there
is no provision for printing or
disc access as with Specmaker or
Lerm's SAMTAPE so it will not be
of any use with utilities like a
wordprocessor.It is really meant
for use on games and to overcome
the problems of tape loading.
                        - Brian

12th May 1991

Dear Ron & Brian,

What a brills-ville spiffing new
look! What an absolutely first
class publication you are. In
fact all of you at 'Chezron
Software' are a God-send to your
readership and an example to
others on customer care. I think
the new look is excellent and
all the better even with the...
how should I say?...old-hat look
still included in case fellow
readers don't quite agree.

This bit is aimed at you BC. I
recently had a letter of reply
back from Mr. Stevens of the
'SCPDSA' and apart from being
upset with the way I worded my
letter of discontent over his
handling of the so-called "free"
disk, tells me that: (A) it was
only very lightly protected, and
very easy to crack (to most
budding hackers and programmers
yes? but to the likes of me, no)
and (B) the 'SCPDSA' disk is
"copyrighted property." I ask
this -where is this copyright he
refers to? I can fully
understand the original authors
holding that, (I thought they
are supposed to relinquish any
rights anyhow otherwise it does
not become 'PD'?) but the
'SCPDSA'...no!

There certainly is no copyright
stamped on the label that
accompanied the disk, nor can I
for the life of me find one
anywhere in the running of the
demos. He made no mention of it
in his advert, so I simply ask
...where is it??!!

He says that to date only two
people have been unhappy with
the protection on the disk (I am
one!) and that he has had many a
letter of goodwill praise for
making the protection as he puts
it "...both enjoyable and easy
to crack!...", I'm sure???!!!

I found his letter in complete
contradiction of everything he
stands for and would like to


know from other readers if they
also found his interpretation of
'PD' as contradictive, and the
protection both as easy to crack
and unnecessary? Do you agree
BC? I know you said that you
spent a considerable amount of
time trying to crack it.

I have been trying to find a
re-inking service in the UK that
does 4-colour ribbon re-inking,
and can at last say that a firm
in Wales will be operating such
a service from mid May though
I have yet to find out exactly
how much and how many ribbons
can or have to be sent. So I
shall hopefully try to find out
for next time as re-inking must
be cheaper than buying them.

I know of a place that sells
LC10C type for `24.95 for 5 (inc
p&p) but the average going is in
the region of `7-`8.00 each.
Re-inking has got to be a more
viable alternative in the long
term. You could obtain a special
machine for around `193.00 (inc
of inks) to do the job yourself
...no? ok!!

Re-ink service:
DATA-ACCESS, UNIT 14, 100
TROSTRE ROAD, LLANELLI,DYFED
SA15 2AE. TEL:(0554) 771977

Mail order for ribbons:
BEST PRICES,(MAIL-ORDER
MARKETING & DISTRIBUTION),UNIT
A, GRAFTON PLACE, WORTHING,WEST
SUSSEX, BN11 1QX. TEL:(0903)
700714

Have you still been unable to
review the new 'SINCLAIR & SAM
COMPUTING' yet? I have my first
issue now and its pretty good to
say the least. There are 48
pages mostly SAM coverage, with
Spectrum coverage a close second
and last with only 3 pages to
itself is the QL. It's very good
all round, very nicely typed and
put together - a very good mag
for a first attempt.


Mr.Garner deserves a mention
here for his positive attitude
regarding customer care to his
subscribers in replacing my
missing issue without any undue
hassle or being discourteous in
any way - well done!

I'd like to remark to Mr.
K.A.Schimmel from Nottingham who
mentioned obtaining "composite
video signals" from computers -
was to tune the computer to the
'VCR'.True! but what you are in
fact doing Mr. Schimmel is not
tuning to receive a composite
video signal, but an "RF" (Radio
Frequency) signal, as all
computers generate a raw
untouched composite signal
inside them prior to being
converted by the "RF Modulator"
also in the computer, or in the
case of the SAM, in the power
supply. As all TV tuners like in
the VCR receive "RF" off-air
signals, as I believe there is
no known way to transmit
raw-untouched video signals over
the air waves?

So, what your computer is doing
is first generating the
composite (raw-video) signal,
converting it in the "RF"
modulator, transmitting it along
the "UHF" (ultra-high-frequency)
lead (as supplied) to the VCR's
"RF-in" socket. Then the VCR
re-converts it back to its
original form ie: composite -
which is what you record!

This whole process has the
unfortunate side effect of
"picture quality loss" due to
the signal being converted then
re-converted etc! That's why the
good old boys at 'MGT' gave our
SAM his very own 'SCART'socket
to save all the hassle of this
plus tuning etc, etc!

Unlike the poor Speccy who
unfortunately has no such socket
at his disposal? (Aaawhh!!)

             Cheers,
  and best regards to you all,

          Si Greenfield.

Brian Cavers to Simon Greenfield

There is no legal definition of
"PUBLIC DOMAIN" in this country
nor is there any authoritative
body with the power to insist
how it should be defined. I have
seen many varying definitions of
it as well as the word FREEWARE.

I think in the 16-bit market it
is most commonly held to mean
that the author DOES retain the
copyright but gives permission
for ANYONE to copy the software
and to give copies away to other
users so long as no charge is
made for the software itself but
it is acceptable to charge for
the service (e.g., cost of the
disc, postage, etc.).

When we began what I believe was
the first drive magazine in 1987
(no, I won't argue if someone
knows of another earlier one - I
really don't care -it's not that
important) I chose to use the
term FREEWARE as a synonym for
public domain because, at that
time, your average Spectrum user
had never heard of public domain
and may possibly have been
puzzled by it(I thought anyway).
So, our FREEWARE can be regarded
as the same definition I gave on
the last page for public domain
(may be different to PC users!).

There is no rule about marking
copyright or public domain. The
author of a work has copyright.
It does not need registration in

this country nor (I believe) is
it necessary to mark the work
as copyright (in this country).
However, it is RECOMMENDED as it
may possibly help in litigation.

I rarely bother to mark our own
material with a copyright sign
because litigation is more
appropriate to a big-selling
piece of software worth many
thousands or even millions of
pounds but I do put our name and
address at the top of listings
usually just as a service to
anyone who sees the program,
likes it, and would like to see
more (O.K. - yes, so we can make
more money!)but if a contributor
puts a copyright sign in his or
her program, I leave it there.

Contributors to OUTLET keep the
copyright in the work. If they
tell me they want it to be made
public domain or FREEWARE then I
mark the title page.

That's how we do it. So,although
I like programs to be open and
user-friendly and unprotected
and therefore cannot agree with
SCPDSA's policies, they are
entitled to impose whatever
restrictions they want. Live and
let live, say I.

Regarding leaving a full address
and date - please repeat IN EACH
LETTER as I may not remember! I
don't think Ron's database is
flagged for such things and we
have nearly 3,000 names on it!

Just to clarify our policy on
full addresses - we do not
publish full addresses without
permission but just the area so
others may know from what part
of the country a reader comes.
This both saves space and is a
courtesy to the reader who may
not wish to have others contact
him or her direct. I think that
is in line with most newspapers
and magazines.

As for contributions, we make a
payment automatically UNLESS the
contributor waives it. Some
prefer to extend their OUTLET
subscription in lieu! Some have
have had free OUTLETs for yonks!
- They just contribute something
now and again!       - Brian

From P.C.Glover, BIRMINGHAM

Dear Ron and Brian,

Thanks very much for the
up-dated copy of OUTWRITE and
the manual. I'm returning the
original copy I bought at the
Birmingham All Formats Fair as
I'm sure you can recycle it, and
also save on the labelling.

OUTWRITE is proving to be very
good indeed as it's very easy to
use. It's good to see a program
make such good use of the
function keys, and the extra
fonts now available are very
good. I hope the program sells
well as it is priced so
reasonably.

I know your reviews of the
computer press are variable, due
to erratic publication dates,
but have you considered giving
MICRO COMPUTER MART a mention? I
often buy it to browse through,
and the Sam Coupe has received
some favourable remarks in
recent issues. I wrote to Nigel
Cummings, the Editor, and he
wrote back saying:


"I will confirm that we intend
to offer more coverage on the
Sam range and associated
products. Regarding a regular
Sam column, however, we shall
have to wait and see how well
this re-launched' product
performs in the market place".

MICRO COMPUTER MART seems to be
one of the few printed
publications that's taking Sam
seriously. I hope a few more
will do so if Sam's sales rise
and hardware and software
increase in quantity.

All the very best to you both,

         Phil Glover

P.S. I think the new 'Sam'-look
editorial and feature of OUTLET
are superb. I think some people
may have found the OUTLET looked
rather 'Spectrummy' with its
page layout, and I think the new
style should prove very popular.

Brian Cavers to Phil Glover

Thanks, Phil. Yes, although it's
interesting to remember that the
standard default screen display
on the SAM COUPE is 32 columns!
Many programs written ON the SAM
FOR the SAM use the normal SAM
screen and look just like a
Spectrum! It's a funny old world
innit?

We've now abandoned our regular
monthly look at the magazines
unless the situation changes at
some future date. Micro Computer
Mart was never included because
it is fortnightly and the issue
reviewed would be off the news-
agents shelves by the time you
read about it in OUTLET! - Brian.

DUMP and "dumpld"

```text
      POKE 83241,0,27,75
      POKE 83249,0,27,75
```

Press CONTINUE (F5) and "Save to Tape/Disc?" prompts appear but I suggest you DO NOT re-save yet - not until you are completely happy with the pokes.

```text
   -   -   -   -   -   -   -
```

These pokes have been thoroughly tested with both a 512k and a 256k SAM, the latter with a 1meg extension and I strongly expect them to work equally well with other "Epson-compatible" double- density printers. Note my use of

quotes on the "Epson-compatible" bit... as there are even Epsons which aren't "Epson-compatible" is it any wonder there is so much confusion about the matter?

A lot of the confusion arises because of the large group of double-density printers which are "compatible" in all respects except those commands which are specifically quad-density. The Shinwa CP80 series fall in this group and I believe the Mannes- man MT80 is another.

The significant command missing from this group is the ESC 27, "*",mode command... the double- density printers are restricted to ESC "K" and "L" - single and double density, 8-bit graphics.

Unfortunately, both "dumpld" and "FLASH" rely on the "*" command, as does Steve Nutting's "Filer" (incidentally, "Filer" is THE definitive database - far above anything yet produced for the SAM coupe... or the Spectrum).

However back to the subject... the pokes above deal with FLASH and "dumpld" and as "Filer" uses the latter it is an easy task to convert it.  There are two BASIC programs... so just load "auto", enter BASIC, edit line 12100 and immediately following the LOAD "dump" CODE add... :POKE SVAR 31,4: POKE SVAR 35,75

Re-Enter the line and SAVE OVER "auto" LINE 65000.

The 2nd BASIC file is "create" and the same two POKES are added to line 120, again following the LOAD "dump" CODE. This time SAVE OVER "create" LINE 10.

I don't know about the Mannesman group of printers but the Shinwa CPA80s have a single dot density of 80 per inch compared with the Epson's 60 and this gives a dump which is about 25% narrow. This can be offset by having smaller line-feeds. I haven't, as yet, solved this problem with the "dumpld" code but "FLASH" can be amended at the same time as the previous pokes.... POKE 83238,27,51,n POKE 83246,27,51,n when "n" is the number of 216ths required for each line feed.

The present feed is the equiva- lent of 24 but I suggest 22 -try 21 as well. I must warn however that the overprinting of just 2 or 3/216ths can mar the finished appearance of certain intricate patterns so use this with care.

This final poke will be useful with both quad-density and double-density printers alike. Have you noticed that before a "FLASH" dump is made the printer feeds up three lines. If you wish to stop, or even reduce, this feed just add the following poke with the others. It is...

POKE 83235,0,0,0

If you wish only to get rid of two of the feeds, leaving just the one, then poke only two of the 0's (or poke one only and leave two line-feeds).

NOTE...  ALL THE 0s QUOTED IN THIS ARTICLE ARE THE FIGURE "0".

I can't finish without a mention of the part played in sorting out these printer dump problems by a SAM-owning friend who lives nearby and visits me regularly. He is Fred Hindle and the pair of us have been trying for well a year to find an answer to our problems.

We had both of us spoken to Alan Miles & Bruce Gordon at MGT on several occasions but were given only pokes and hints which were useless. I had also been in touch with Steve Nutting on a couple of occasions - all to no avail. Finally, as a last resort Fred wrote to Dr. Andy Wright who put us on the right track by providing the addresses to search. We really are grateful Dr. Andy, thank-you.

I know of four SAM owners within a mile of here and our combined ages are above 260 yrs. (no - we weren't born in 1731... it was just after). Three of us are subscribers to OUTLET - The Three Wise Men... but not so old when we have OUTLET.

- Colin Demaline

### От: Colin Demaline, LANCS.

### GRAPHIC DUMPS ON SHINWA CPA80's & Other Double-Density Printers.
--------------------------------

Сначала поуки — разговоры потом...

#### DUMP и "dumpld"

Сразу после загрузки «dumpld» от MGT ИЛИ прямо перед вводом команды DUMP...

```text
        POKE SVAR 31,4
        POKE SVAR 35,75
```

Если заменить последнюю 75 на 76, получится дамп двойной плотности половинной ширины.

#### "FLASH" — ВСЕ ДАМПЫ
Загрузите «Flash» и по запросу «Save to Tape?» УДАЛИТЕ левую кавычку и введите «STOP». Теперь наберите:

```text
      POKE 83241,0,27,75
      POKE 83249,0,27,75
```

Нажмите CONTINUE (F5), и появится запрос «Save to Tape/Disc?», но я советую ПОКА НЕ пересохранять — подождите, пока полностью не убедитесь, что поуки работают как надо.
   -   -   -   -   -   -   -
Эти поуки были тщательно протестированы как на SAM 512k, так и на 256k, причем на последнем — с расширением памяти на 1 МБ, и я абсолютно уверен, что они будут так же хорошо работать и с другими «Epson-совместимыми» принтерами двойной плотности. Заметьте, я беру в кавычки «Epson-совместимый»... ведь существуют даже принтеры Epson, которые не являются «Epson-совместимыми» — стоит ли удивляться, что вокруг этого столько неразберихи?

Большая часть путаницы возникает из-за обширной группы принтеров двойной плотности, которые «совместимы» во всем, кроме команд четверичной плотности (quad-density). Серия Shinwa CP80 относится к этой группе, и я полагаю, что Mannesman MT80 — тоже.

Главная недостающая команда в этой группе — это ESC 27, "*",mode... принтеры двойной плотности ограничены командами ESC "K" и "L" — 8-битная графика одинарной и двойной плотности.

К сожалению, и «dumpld», и «FLASH» опираются на команду «*», так же как и «Filer» от Steve Nutting (к слову, «Filer» — это ЭТАЛОННАЯ база данных, стоящая на голову выше всего, что до сих пор создавалось для SAM Coupe... или для Spectrum).

Однако вернемся к теме... вышеприведенные поуки относятся к FLASH и «dumpld», а поскольку «Filer» использует последний, адаптировать его проще простого. Там две бейсик-программы... загрузите «auto», войдите в BASIC, отредактируйте строку 12100 и сразу после LOAD "dump" CODE добавьте:

```text
:POKE SVAR 31,4: POKE SVAR 35,75
```

Заново введите строку и выполните SAVE OVER "auto" LINE 65000.

Второй файл бейсика — «create», и те же два POKE добавляются в строку 120, снова вслед за LOAD "dump" CODE. На этот раз сохраните через SAVE OVER "create" LINE 10.

Не знаю насчет группы принтеров Mannesman, но у серии Shinwa CPA80 одинарная плотность составляет 80 точек на дюйм по сравнению с 60 у Epson, из-за чего дамп получается примерно на 25% уже. Это можно компенсировать уменьшением шага подачи строк. Эту проблему в коде «dumpld» я пока не решил, но во «FLASH» ее можно исправить одновременно с предыдущими поуками:

```text
   POKE 83238,27,51,n
   POKE 83246,27,51,n
```

где «n» — количество 216-х долей дюйма для каждого перевода строки.

Текущий шаг эквивалентен 24, но я рекомендую 22 — попробуйте также 21. Должен, однако, предупредить, что перекрытие всего в 2 или 3/216 дюйма может испортить вид некоторых сложных узоров, так что пользуйтесь аккуратно.

Этот последний поук пригодится владельцам как четверичной, так и двойной плотности. Замечали ли вы, что перед началом дампа во «FLASH» принтер протягивает бумагу на три строки вверх? Если вы хотите прекратить эту протяжку или хотя бы уменьшить ее, просто добавьте к остальным следующий поук:

```text
    POKE 83235,0,0,0
```

Если вы хотите убрать только две протяжки, оставив одну, измените только два ноля (или один, чтобы осталось две строки).

Когда мы в 1987 году запустили, как я полагаю, первый дисковый журнал (нет, я не буду спорить, если кто-то знает более ранний — мне всё равно, это не так важно), я решил использовать термин FREEWARE как синоним public domain, потому что в то время обычный пользователь Spectrum никогда не слышал о public domain и мог быть озадачен (я так думал). Так что наш FREEWARE можно считать тем же самым определением, что я дал на последней странице для public domain (это может отличаться от того, как считают пользователи PC!).

Нет никаких правил относительно маркировки авторского права или public domain. Автор произведения обладает авторским правом. В нашей стране оно не требует регистрации, и (я считаю) не обязательно помечать работу как «авторское право» (в нашей стране). Однако это РЕКОМЕНДУЕТСЯ, так как может помочь в судебных разбирательствах.

Я редко утруждаю себя пометкой нашего материала знаком авторского права, потому что суды больше подходят для крупнобюджетного софта, стоящего миллионы фунтов. Но я обычно указываю наши имя и адрес в начале листингов — просто как услугу для тех, кто увидит программу, она им понравится, и они захотят увидеть больше (окей, да, чтобы мы могли заработать больше денег!). Но если автор добавляет знак копирайта в свою программу, я его оставляю.

Авторы, присылающие материалы в OUTLET, сохраняют авторские права на свои работы. Если они говорят мне, что хотят сделать её общественным достоянием (public domain) или FREEWARE, я указываю это на титульной странице.

Вот как мы это делаем. Так что, хотя мне нравятся открытые, удобные для пользователя программы без защиты, и я не могу согласиться с политикой SCPDSA, они имеют право устанавливать любые ограничения. Живи и давай жить другим, как говорится.

Что касается указания полного адреса и даты — пожалуйста, повторяйте это В КАЖДОМ ПИСЬМЕ, я могу не запомнить! Не думаю, что база данных Рона помечена для таких вещей, а у нас в ней почти 3000 имен!

Просто чтобы прояснить нашу политику насчет полных адресов — мы не публикуем полные адреса без разрешения, указываем лишь район, чтобы другие знали, из какой части страны наш читатель. Это и место экономит, и является данью вежливости по отношению к автору письма, который, возможно, не хочет, чтобы с ним или с ней связывались напрямую. Думаю, это вполне в духе большинства газет и журналов.

Что касается материалов для публикации, мы автоматически производим выплату, ЕСЛИ ТОЛЬКО автор сам от нее не откажется. Некоторые предпочитают вместо этого продлить подписку на OUTLET! Кое-кто получает OUTLET бесплатно уже целую вечность! — Просто присылая что-нибудь время от времени! — Brian
